absorption-variable-costing-inventory-pr.shows: Make more than you sell and absorption costing parks fixed overhead in inventory with every unsold unit, so it reports more profit than variable costing
absorption-variable-costing-inventory-pr.subject: finance
absorption-variable-costing-inventory-pr.title: Absorption vs variable costing: profit and inventory

accretion-dilution.shows: Acquirer EPS before and after a deal as the stock/cash mix, the price paid and synergies change
accretion-dilution.subject: finance
accretion-dilution.title: Accretion / dilution: acquirer EPS after a deal

accrual-vs-cash-accounting.shows: Move the month the work is done and how long the customer takes to pay: cash basis follows the money, accrual follows the work, and the gap is a receivable, deferred revenue or a prepaid expense
accrual-vs-cash-accounting.subject: finance
accrual-vs-cash-accounting.title: Accrual vs cash accounting

accuracy-vs-precision-targets.shows: Move the mean and widen the spread: accuracy is how far the average lands from the bullseye, precision is how tightly the shots group
accuracy-vs-precision-targets.subject: stats
accuracy-vs-precision-targets.title: Accuracy vs precision

actin-driven-cell-migration.shows: Step through protrude, adhere, contract and release; slide polymerization and rearward flow to see that the front moves at their difference
actin-driven-cell-migration.subject: biology
actin-driven-cell-migration.title: Actin-driven cell migration

actin-filament-polymerization.shows: Slide the actin concentration and the time: filaments form only after a slow nucleation lag, grow fast, then level off where free actin has fallen to the critical concentration; seeds skip the lag
actin-filament-polymerization.subject: biology
actin-filament-polymerization.title: Actin polymerization: lag, growth, plateau

actin-filament-treadmilling.shows: Slide the free ATP-actin concentration: each end grows at k_on c - k_off; between the two critical concentrations the barbed end gains while the pointed end loses, and at 0.17 µM the two cancel so the filament keeps its length while subunits flow through it
actin-filament-treadmilling.subject: biology
actin-filament-treadmilling.title: Actin treadmilling

active-vs-passive-immunity.shows: Pick an example: active immunity means your own B cells make antibody and memory cells, slowly at first; passive immunity is borrowed antibody that protects at once, fades with a half-life of weeks and leaves no memory
active-vs-passive-immunity.subject: biology
active-vs-passive-immunity.title: Active vs passive immunity

acute-inflammation.shows: Step through a splinter wound: the alarm, wider vessels (red, warm), leaky vessels (swollen, painful), neutrophils crossing the vessel wall to the bacteria, then cleanup and resolution
acute-inflammation.subject: biology
acute-inflammation.title: Acute inflammation

alternative-rna-splicing-isoforms.shows: Pick a splicing pattern and slide Ψ: the same pre-mRNA is spliced two ways, giving mRNA isoforms of different lengths, and Ψ is the share that keeps the alternative piece
alternative-rna-splicing-isoforms.subject: biology
alternative-rna-splicing-isoforms.title: Alternative splicing patterns

alternative-rna-splicing-protein-isoform.shows: Switch the three optional exons on and off: in-frame exons add or remove protein domains, while an exon whose length is not a multiple of 3 shifts the reading frame into an early stop codon
alternative-rna-splicing-protein-isoform.subject: biology
alternative-rna-splicing-protein-isoform.title: Splicing makes protein isoforms

amino-acid-side-chain-properties.shows: Pick an amino acid and a pH: side chains sort into nonpolar, polar, acidic and basic, from hydrophobic to hydrophilic, and the ionizable ones gain or lose charge with pH
amino-acid-side-chain-properties.subject: biology
amino-acid-side-chain-properties.title: Amino acid side chains: properties

amino-acid-structure.shows: Slide the pH: every amino acid is an alpha carbon carrying an amino group, a carboxyl group, an H and a side chain, and the two groups gain or lose H+ to give a cation, a zwitterion or an anion
amino-acid-structure.subject: biology
amino-acid-structure.title: Amino acid structure and charge

amino-acids-and-peptide-bonds.shows: Step through a condensation: the carboxyl OH of one amino acid and an H from the next one's amino group leave as water, and the new C–N peptide bond joins them into a dipeptide with an N-terminus and a C-terminus
amino-acids-and-peptide-bonds.subject: biology
amino-acids-and-peptide-bonds.title: Amino acids and the peptide bond

angular-frequency-relation.shows: Slide f and t: a point turning f times a second sweeps 2π rad per turn, so ω = 2πf rad/s, and one turn takes T = 1/f
angular-frequency-relation.subject: physics
angular-frequency-relation.title: Angular frequency and period

animal-cell-cytokinesis-cleavage.shows: Step through cytokinesis in an animal cell: a contractile ring of actin and myosin forms over the spindle midzone and pinches the cell in two; move the spindle to make unequal daughters
animal-cell-cytokinesis-cleavage.subject: biology
animal-cell-cytokinesis-cleavage.title: Cytokinesis: the cleavage furrow

animal-cell-junction-functions.shows: Pick a junction: tight junctions seal, adherens junctions and desmosomes hold cells together through actin and keratin, gap junctions let small molecules pass, hemidesmosomes anchor cells to the basal lamina
animal-cell-junction-functions.subject: biology
animal-cell-junction-functions.title: Cell junctions and what they do

animal-cell-structure-and-function.shows: Pick an organelle to see where it sits and what it does; switch the cell type to see structure follow function, from enzyme-exporting pancreas cells to mitochondria-packed heart muscle
animal-cell-structure-and-function.subject: biology
animal-cell-structure-and-function.title: Animal cell: organelles and their jobs

animal-cell-tonicity-comparison.shows: Slide the salt outside a red blood cell: hypotonic swells it until it bursts, isotonic leaves it alone, hypertonic shrivels it; urea raises osmolarity but crosses the membrane, so it does not count toward tonicity
animal-cell-tonicity-comparison.subject: biology
animal-cell-tonicity-comparison.title: Tonicity: a cell in three solutions

anova-decomposition.shows: Drag any point: each value's gap from the grand mean splits into a between-group part and a within-group part, and F weighs one against the other
anova-decomposition.subject: stats
anova-decomposition.title: ANOVA: between vs within

anova-interaction-plot.shows: Pick a pattern: parallel lines mean no interaction, spreading lines a non-crossover one, crossing lines a crossover one; the interaction is the difference between the two simple effects
anova-interaction-plot.subject: stats
anova-interaction-plot.title: Two-way ANOVA interaction plot

antibody-heavy-light-chain-fab-fc-struct.shows: Color the IgG by chain, by variable and constant domain, or by Fab and Fc, then digest it with papain or pepsin to see which pieces come apart
antibody-heavy-light-chain-fab-fc-struct.subject: biology
antibody-heavy-light-chain-fab-fc-struct.title: Antibody chains, Fab and Fc

antibody-specificity-and-antigen-neutral.shows: Pick an antibody and add more of it: only one whose binding site fits the spike's epitope binds, and a virus is neutralized only when every one of its spikes is covered
antibody-specificity-and-antigen-neutral.subject: biology
antibody-specificity-and-antigen-neutral.title: Antibody specificity and neutralization

antibody-structure.shows: Switch the class: every antibody is built from Y units of two heavy and two light chains, and the classes differ in how many units, which heavy chain, and the hinge
antibody-structure.subject: biology
antibody-structure.title: Antibody structure and classes

antigen-presentation-pathways.shows: Pick a route and step through it: inside proteins go proteasome, ER and MHC I to CD8 T cells; engulfed proteins go endosome and MHC II to CD4 T cells; dendritic cells cross outside antigen onto MHC I
antigen-presentation-pathways.subject: biology
antigen-presentation-pathways.title: Antigen presentation: MHC I and MHC II

antigen-specific-clonal-selection-and-ex.shows: Pick an antigen and step through: out of a pool of lymphocytes with different receptors only the matching one is selected, it divides into a clone, and the clone splits into effector and memory cells
antigen-specific-clonal-selection-and-ex.subject: biology
antigen-specific-clonal-selection-and-ex.title: Clonal selection and expansion

antiparallel-dna-strands.shows: The two strands of DNA run opposite ways, 5′→3′ against 3′→5′: read the partner 5′→3′ and you get the reverse complement; A–T pairs hold by 2 hydrogen bonds, G–C by 3
antiparallel-dna-strands.subject: biology
antiparallel-dna-strands.title: Antiparallel DNA strands

apoptosis.shows: Pick the trigger and step through apoptosis: damage inside releases cytochrome c from mitochondria, a death ligand outside builds the DISC, and both switch on caspases that package the cell neatly for phagocytes
apoptosis.subject: biology
apoptosis.title: Apoptosis: intrinsic and extrinsic pathways

apoptosis-versus-necrosis.shows: Step through two cell deaths side by side: apoptosis shrinks the cell and packages it into sealed bodies that are eaten quietly; necrosis swells it until it bursts and inflames the tissue
apoptosis-versus-necrosis.subject: biology
apoptosis-versus-necrosis.title: Apoptosis versus necrosis

arithmetic-mean.shows: Change the three values: the mean is the equal share of their total, and the balance point where the deviations cancel
arithmetic-mean.subject: stats
arithmetic-mean.title: The arithmetic mean

atp-driven-active-transport.shows: Step through one cycle of the Na⁺/K⁺ pump (3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in per ATP) and change the gradients and membrane voltage to see what the cycle costs against the energy one ATP supplies
atp-driven-active-transport.subject: biology
atp-driven-active-transport.title: Active transport: the sodium-potassium pump

autocorrelation.shows: Pick a pattern and a lag: r_k correlates the series with itself k steps later, and the correlogram shows it for every lag
autocorrelation.subject: stats
autocorrelation.title: Autocorrelation and the correlogram

autocrine-cell-signaling.shows: Step through a cell secreting a ligand that binds its own receptors; raise the ligand level or the receptors' Kd to change how many are occupied, or block the receptors to break the loop
autocrine-cell-signaling.subject: biology
autocrine-cell-signaling.title: Autocrine signaling: a cell talks to itself

autophagy-lysosome-recycling.shows: Step through autophagy: a double membrane wraps worn-out parts, fuses with a lysosome, digests them and returns the building blocks; switch fed to starved to see mTORC1 release the brake
autophagy-lysosome-recycling.subject: biology
autophagy-lysosome-recycling.title: Autophagy: recycling through the lysosome

average-speed-distance-time.shows: Set two legs of a trip: the average speed is the slope of the start-to-finish chord, total distance over total time, not the mean of the two speeds
average-speed-distance-time.subject: physics
average-speed-distance-time.title: Average speed: distance over time

b-cell-plasma-cell-antibody-secretion.shows: Step from antigen binding through T-cell help and clonal expansion to plasma cells; set divisions, plasma share and rate to see the antibody output
b-cell-plasma-cell-antibody-secretion.subject: biology
b-cell-plasma-cell-antibody-secretion.title: B cell to plasma cell: antibody secretion

bacterial-transformation-antibiotic-sele.shows: Step through ice, heat shock, recovery and plating; change the DNA, the efficiency or the plate to see which cells grow and how many colonies you get
bacterial-transformation-antibiotic-sele.subject: biology
bacterial-transformation-antibiotic-sele.title: Transformation and antibiotic selection

bacterial-transformation-free-dna-uptake.shows: Step a cell through taking up a free plasmid, then set the colonies, the DNA and the share plated to get the transformation efficiency
bacterial-transformation-free-dna-uptake.subject: biology
bacterial-transformation-free-dna-uptake.title: Bacterial transformation: taking up free DNA

basal-body-cilium-anchoring.shows: Drag the cut up a cilium: 9 triplets and a cartwheel in the basal body, transition fibers docking it to the membrane, 9 doublets in the transition zone, then a 9+2 or 9+0 axoneme and singlets at the tip
basal-body-cilium-anchoring.subject: biology
basal-body-cilium-anchoring.title: Basal body: how a cilium is anchored

bayes-theorem.shows: Set the prior and the two likelihoods: the shaded blocks are the ways B can happen, and P(A|B) is the share of them that came from A
bayes-theorem.subject: stats
bayes-theorem.title: Bayes' theorem as areas

bayesian-beta-binomial-updating.shows: Set a Beta prior and add successes and failures: the posterior Beta(α + s, β + f) lands between the prior and the data, weighted by how much of each you have
bayesian-beta-binomial-updating.subject: stats
bayesian-beta-binomial-updating.title: Beta-binomial Bayesian updating

binomial-distribution.shows: Set the number of trials and the success chance: the bars are the probability of each number of successes, centred on np
binomial-distribution.subject: stats
binomial-distribution.title: Binomial distribution

biological-calibration-curve-and-unknown.shows: Slide the unknown's absorbance: read across to the standard line and down to its concentration, then multiply back by the dilution
biological-calibration-curve-and-unknown.subject: stats
biological-calibration-curve-and-unknown.title: Standard curve: reading an unknown

biological-measurement-accuracy-and-prec.shows: Weigh repeated 100 µL dispenses: bias moves the whole cluster away from the true volume (accuracy), spread widens it (precision)
biological-measurement-accuracy-and-prec.subject: stats
biological-measurement-accuracy-and-prec.title: Pipette accuracy and precision

biological-outlier-effects-on-mean-and-m.shows: Drag one plate's colony count far from its replicates: the mean follows it without limit, the median barely moves
biological-outlier-effects-on-mean-and-m.subject: stats
biological-outlier-effects-on-mean-and-m.title: One odd plate: mean vs median

biological-random-sampling-and-selection.shows: Sample snails at random or by picking the easiest to spot: random samples scatter around the true mean, biased ones land too high every time
biological-random-sampling-and-selection.subject: stats
biological-random-sampling-and-selection.title: Random sampling vs selection bias

biotechnology.shows: Pick the enzyme that cuts the plasmid and the one that cuts the gene, then step through pairing, ligation, transformation and expression
biotechnology.subject: biology
biotechnology.title: Recombinant DNA: putting a gene into a plasmid

blue-white-screening.shows: Set how many plasmids carry the insert and what is in the plate: white colonies have the insert, blue ones are empty vector
blue-white-screening.subject: biology
blue-white-screening.title: Blue-white screening

bootstrap-distribution.shows: Resample the data with replacement again and again: the spread of the recomputed statistic is its standard error, and its middle 95% is an interval
bootstrap-distribution.subject: stats
bootstrap-distribution.title: The bootstrap distribution

box-plot.shows: Pick a shape for class B: the box is the middle half (Q1 to Q3), the line the median, the whiskers run to the last score inside the 1.5 IQR fences
box-plot.subject: stats
box-plot.title: Box plots: reading shape and spread

calcium-second-messenger-relay.shows: Step through the relay from a Gq-coupled receptor to IP₃, an ER calcium release that lifts cytosolic Ca²⁺ tenfold, calmodulin and PKC, and the pumps that end the signal; block the pumps and the signal cannot switch off
calcium-second-messenger-relay.subject: biology
calcium-second-messenger-relay.title: Calcium as a second messenger

camp-second-messenger-relay.shows: Raise the hormone, slow the phosphodiesterase or add cholera toxin: adenylyl cyclase fills the cAMP pool, PDE drains it, and the level where the two match decides how much PKA turns on
camp-second-messenger-relay.subject: biology
camp-second-messenger-relay.title: cAMP: a second messenger in balance

cancer-cell-cycle-failure.shows: Pick the problem a dividing cell meets and compare a normal cell, whose checkpoint stops it, with a cancer cell, whose broken checkpoint lets it divide into daughters with a mutation, a broken chromosome or the wrong number
cancer-cell-cycle-failure.subject: biology
cancer-cell-cycle-failure.title: Cancer: when a checkpoint fails

cell-communication.shows: Pick contact, synaptic, paracrine or endocrine signaling: diffusion time grows with distance squared, which is why far signals need blood or an axon, and only cells with the matching receptor respond
cell-communication.subject: biology
cell-communication.title: How cells signal: by distance

cell-cycle.shows: Slide the clock through G1, S, G2 and mitosis: the DNA per cell climbs from 2C to 4C during S and halves at division, and changing G1 changes how fast the cells multiply
cell-cycle.subject: biology
cell-cycle.title: The cell cycle in hours

cell-cycle-and-regulation.shows: Slide through the cycle: CDK levels stay flat while cyclins D, E, A and B rise and fall in turn, each switching on the next step; remove growth factors or block APC/C to see where the cycle stops
cell-cycle-and-regulation.subject: biology
cell-cycle-and-regulation.title: Cyclins and CDKs drive the cycle

cell-cycle-checkpoint-decision-map.shows: Give the cell a problem: it runs round G1, S, G2 and M until the first checkpoint that says no, and the map shows why it stops and what happens next
cell-cycle-checkpoint-decision-map.subject: biology
cell-cycle-checkpoint-decision-map.title: Cell cycle checkpoints: go or stop

cell-cycle-checkpoints.shows: Step through the G1/S, G2/M and spindle checkpoints: each senses one problem and brakes one switch (cyclin E–CDK2, cyclin B–CDK1, APC/C); turn the problem off and the switch flips and the cell moves on
cell-cycle-checkpoints.subject: biology
cell-cycle-checkpoints.title: The three cell cycle checkpoints

cell-junctions.shows: Pick a junction: see where it sits on the cell, what crosses the gap, what it grips inside, and whether it seals, anchors or lets molecules through
cell-junctions.subject: biology
cell-junctions.title: Cell junctions, layer by layer

cell-membrane-transport.shows: Pick a mechanism and set the concentrations: passive transport only runs downhill (straight-line or saturating), a pump keeps moving solute in against the gradient by spending ATP
cell-membrane-transport.subject: biology
cell-membrane-transport.title: Membrane transport: diffusion, carriers, pumps

cell-organelles.shows: Switch between an animal and a plant cell and light up what only that type has (wall, chloroplasts, central vacuole versus centrioles and lysosomes) or what both share
cell-organelles.subject: biology
cell-organelles.title: Animal and plant cell organelles

cell-receptor-location-comparison.shows: Pick a hormone and a time: water-soluble ones stop at surface receptors and act in seconds; steroids cross the membrane, meet receptors inside and change genes over hours
cell-receptor-location-comparison.subject: biology
cell-receptor-location-comparison.title: Surface versus intracellular receptors

cell-signaling-pathway.shows: Step through epinephrine signaling in a liver cell: receptor, G protein, cAMP, a kinase cascade and glycogen breakdown, with the amplification at each stage and the switch-off at the end
cell-signaling-pathway.subject: biology
cell-signaling-pathway.title: Cell signaling: from receptor to response

cell-surface-movement-and-cytoskeleton.shows: Pick a surface structure: see how it moves (or doesn't), the cytoskeleton inside it in cross-section, and which of the three filament types it is built from
cell-surface-movement-and-cytoskeleton.subject: biology
cell-surface-movement-and-cytoskeleton.title: Cilia, flagella, microvilli and crawling

cell-surface-receptor-recognition.shows: Set the ligand's concentration, the receptor's Kd and the ligand's shape: half the receptors fill at [L] = Kd, agonists switch them on, antagonists only block, wrong shapes never bind
cell-surface-receptor-recognition.subject: biology
cell-surface-receptor-recognition.title: Receptor recognition: fit and affinity

cell-surface-recognition-adhesion.shows: Choose the molecule on each cell's surface and the calcium: cells stick only when the molecules recognize each other, and cadherins and selectins also need Ca²⁺
cell-surface-recognition-adhesion.subject: biology
cell-surface-recognition-adhesion.title: Cell surface recognition and adhesion

cell-type-specific-gene-expression.shows: Pick a cell and switch between DNA and mRNA: every cell carries the same genes, but each transcribes the housekeeping genes plus its own tissue-specific ones
cell-type-specific-gene-expression.subject: biology
cell-type-specific-gene-expression.title: Cell-type-specific gene expression

cell-type-specific-transcription-factors.shows: Switch the cell type or add one activator: a gene is transcribed only when the cell has an activator for every control element in its enhancer
cell-type-specific-transcription-factors.subject: biology
cell-type-specific-transcription-factors.title: Cell-type-specific transcription factors

cellular-compartmentalization.shows: Shut the same molecules into a smaller compartment: their concentration rises by one over the volume fraction, so partners kept together meet far more often than they would loose in the whole cell
cellular-compartmentalization.subject: biology
cellular-compartmentalization.title: Compartments concentrate molecules

cellular-structure-and-functions.shows: Pick a job (store DNA, make proteins, make ATP, hold the shape...) and see which structure does it in a bacterium, an animal cell and a plant cell; switch on true scale to see how much bigger eukaryotic cells are
cellular-structure-and-functions.subject: biology
cellular-structure-and-functions.title: Cell structures and their jobs

central-limit-theorem.shows: Pick a population and a sample size: the means of many samples pile up in a normal shape centred on μ, with spread σ/√n, whatever the population looks like
central-limit-theorem.subject: stats
central-limit-theorem.title: The central limit theorem

centripetal-force-mvr.shows: Change the mass, speed and radius: the pull toward the centre grows with m and with v squared, and falls as the circle widens
centripetal-force-mvr.subject: physics
centripetal-force-mvr.title: Centripetal force in circular motion

change-of-basis.shows: The same vector in B-coordinates and in standard coordinates: P, whose columns are b1 and b2, turns one into the other
change-of-basis.subject: linear-algebra
change-of-basis.title: Change of basis

checkpoint-failure-uncontrolled-prolifer.shows: Break the G1/S brake or p53 and follow one cell's descendants: intact checkpoints cap the tissue and remove damaged cells, broken ones let damaged cells multiply
checkpoint-failure-uncontrolled-prolifer.subject: biology
checkpoint-failure-uncontrolled-prolifer.title: Checkpoint failure and uncontrolled growth

chi-square-distribution.shows: Set the degrees of freedom and drag the observed statistic: the shaded right tail is the p-value, and it falls below 5% once you pass the critical value
chi-square-distribution.subject: stats
chi-square-distribution.title: The chi-square distribution and its tail

chi-square-goodness-of-fit.shows: Drag the four counts: each one's gap from the equal-share expectation adds (O − E)²/E to χ², and the tail of χ² with 3 df past that sum is the p-value
chi-square-goodness-of-fit.subject: stats
chi-square-goodness-of-fit.title: Chi-square goodness of fit

chi-square-independence.shows: Change the four counts: if improving does not depend on the group, both groups split at the overall share and O = E in every cell; χ² measures how far they are from that
chi-square-independence.subject: stats
chi-square-independence.title: Chi-square test of independence

cholesterol-membrane-fluidity.shows: Change the temperature and the cholesterol: above the melting point cholesterol stiffens the membrane, below it cholesterol keeps it from freezing into a gel
cholesterol-membrane-fluidity.subject: biology
cholesterol-membrane-fluidity.title: Cholesterol and membrane fluidity

chromatin-accessibility-and-cell-identit.shows: Step a stem cell toward liver, muscle or neuron: the regions of open chromatin narrow to the cell's own program, and that pattern is its identity
chromatin-accessibility-and-cell-identit.subject: biology
chromatin-accessibility-and-cell-identit.title: Open chromatin and cell identity

chromatin-accessibility-gene-expression.shows: Acetylate or deacetylate the histones, methylate the promoter, add or remove the activator: the gene is transcribed only when its promoter is open and an activator binds
chromatin-accessibility-gene-expression.subject: biology
chromatin-accessibility-gene-expression.title: Chromatin accessibility and gene expression

chromosome-sister-chromatid-structure.shows: Step one chromosome from G1 to anaphase and move its centromere: one chromatid becomes two identical sisters joined at the centromere, then they split into two chromosomes
chromosome-sister-chromatid-structure.subject: biology
chromosome-sister-chromatid-structure.title: Chromosome and sister chromatids

cilia-versus-microvilli.shows: Step through a beat: the cilium's 9 + 2 microtubules and dynein make it sweep mucus, while the shorter, thinner microvilli are actin bundles that stay still and add absorbing surface
cilia-versus-microvilli.subject: biology
cilia-versus-microvilli.title: Cilia versus microvilli

ciliary-power-and-recovery-stroke.shows: Play one beat: the cilium sweeps forward straight and tall, then comes back bent and low, so each beat moves fluid one way; make it come back the same way and the flow cancels
ciliary-power-and-recovery-stroke.subject: biology
ciliary-power-and-recovery-stroke.title: Cilia: power and recovery strokes

classification-threshold.shows: Slide the threshold: lowering it catches more true positives but lets in more false alarms; raising it does the reverse, and the ROC dot slides along the curve
classification-threshold.subject: stats
classification-threshold.title: Classification threshold

clonal-selection-and-immune-memory.shows: Slide the day and the second exposure: the first response to an antigen is slow and small, the memory cells it leaves make the second fast and about a hundred times larger, and a new antigen starts from scratch
clonal-selection-and-immune-memory.subject: biology
clonal-selection-and-immune-memory.title: Immune memory: first and second response

coding-strand-mrna-sequence-relationship.shows: Slide along the first codons of beta-globin: the mRNA matches the coding strand letter for letter, with U in place of T
coding-strand-mrna-sequence-relationship.subject: biology
coding-strand-mrna-sequence-relationship.title: Coding strand and mRNA: same sequence, U for T

coding-template-rna-strand-comparison.shows: Slide RNA polymerase along a short gene and compare any two strands: coding and RNA match (U for T), the template pairs with both
coding-template-rna-strand-comparison.subject: biology
coding-template-rna-strand-comparison.title: Coding, template and RNA strands compared

codon-anticodon-pairing.shows: Build a codon base by base: the tRNA's anticodon pairs with it antiparallel and brings the matching amino acid; turn on wobble to see one tRNA read several codons
codon-anticodon-pairing.subject: biology
codon-anticodon-pairing.title: Codon and anticodon pairing

codon-chart.shows: Pick the three bases of an mRNA codon: first base picks the row, second the column, third the line; the codon and every synonym for its amino acid light up
codon-chart.subject: biology
codon-chart.title: The genetic code: reading a codon

cohens-d.shows: Pull the means apart or widen the spread: d counts how many standard deviations separate the groups, and the overlap of the two curves shrinks as d grows
cohens-d.subject: stats
cohens-d.title: Cohen's d: effect size

coin-flipping.shows: Flip a coin n times: the share of heads jumps around at first, then settles toward p inside a funnel that narrows like 1/√n
coin-flipping.subject: stats
coin-flipping.title: Coin flips and the law of large numbers

collision-simulation.shows: Set the carts' velocities and masses: total momentum survives every collision, kinetic energy only an elastic one
collision-simulation.subject: physics
collision-simulation.title: Cart collisions: momentum and energy

column-space.shows: Ax is a combination of the columns of A, so every output lands in Col A: a line, a plane or all of R3 depending on the rank
column-space.subject: linear-algebra
column-space.title: Column space

combination-formula.shows: Pick r of n items: count the ordered picks slot by slot, then divide by r! because every group shows up in r! orders
combination-formula.subject: stats
combination-formula.title: Combinations: choosing r of n

common-normal-intervals.shows: Slide z: the shaded share of a normal curve within ±z standard deviations of the mean, against the 68–95–99.7 rule
common-normal-intervals.subject: stats
common-normal-intervals.title: Normal intervals: the 68–95–99.7 rule

compartment-microenvironments.shows: Pick an organelle: each membrane-bound compartment keeps its own pH and chemistry, from the acidic lysosome (pH 4.7) to the basic mitochondrial matrix (pH 7.9), and the pH line shows how far each sits from the cytosol
compartment-microenvironments.subject: biology
compartment-microenvironments.title: Compartments keep their own chemistry

complement-opsonization-phagocyte-recogn.shows: Step through opsonization: C3 is cut into C3a and C3b, C3b coats the microbe, the phagocyte's complement receptors grip it and it is eaten; with no opsonin the microbe slips away, with IgG as well the grip is strongest
complement-opsonization-phagocyte-recogn.subject: biology
complement-opsonization-phagocyte-recogn.title: Complement opsonization

complementary-base-pairing.shows: Change the GC share and the partner strand: A always pairs with T (or U in RNA) by 2 hydrogen bonds and G with C by 3, a purine with a pyrimidine so every rung is the same width, and more G–C means a stronger duplex
complementary-base-pairing.subject: biology
complementary-base-pairing.title: Complementary base pairing

compound-interest.shows: Slide the rate and the number of periods: the balance grows by 1 + r each period, and the amber interest on interest is what makes the curve bend upward
compound-interest.subject: finance
compound-interest.title: Compound interest

conditional-probability-definition.shows: Set P(B) and P(A ∩ B): knowing B happened shrinks the world to B, and P(A | B) is the share of B where A also happens
conditional-probability-definition.subject: stats
conditional-probability-definition.title: Conditional probability: P(A | B)

confidence-interval-proportion.shows: Slide p̂, n and the confidence level: the interval is p̂ ± z*·SE, wider for more confidence and narrower like 1/√n
confidence-interval-proportion.subject: stats
confidence-interval-proportion.title: Confidence interval for a proportion

confidence-vs-prediction-bands.shows: Around a regression line, the confidence band covers the mean y and the wider prediction band covers one new y; both flare away from x̄
confidence-vs-prediction-bands.subject: stats
confidence-vs-prediction-bands.title: Confidence band vs prediction band

confusion-matrix-metrics.shows: Change the four counts: precision asks how many flagged cases are real, recall how many real cases were caught
confusion-matrix-metrics.subject: stats
confusion-matrix-metrics.title: Confusion matrix: precision, recall and F1

continuous-uniform-distribution.shows: Move a and b: the density stays flat at 1/(b − a) so the area is always 1, and P(c ≤ X ≤ d) is the share of the width [c, d] covers
continuous-uniform-distribution.subject: stats
continuous-uniform-distribution.title: Continuous uniform distribution

coordinates-in-a-basis.shows: The same vector written in two bases; drag the basis and its coordinates change
coordinates-in-a-basis.subject: linear-algebra
coordinates-in-a-basis.title: Coordinates in a basis

correlation.shows: Pick a pattern and add noise: r is the sum of the products (x − x̄)(y − ȳ), scaled to lie between −1 and 1, so its sign says which quadrants the cloud lives in
correlation.subject: stats
correlation.title: Correlation: positive, negative or none

correlation-causation-confounding.shows: Smoking raises both coffee drinking and heart risk, so coffee and risk correlate even when coffee does nothing; split by smoking and the fake part vanishes
correlation-causation-confounding.subject: stats
correlation-causation-confounding.title: Correlation vs causation: a confounder

correlation-matrix.shows: Every pair of variables gets one r: the diagonal is 1, the matrix is symmetric, color shows sign and strength, and each number has the scatter it summarizes
correlation-matrix.subject: stats
correlation-matrix.title: Correlation matrix

crispr-cas9.shows: Step through guide loading, PAM search, the double-strand cut and the repair; switch the goal to see NHEJ knock a gene out or HDR copy in a precise edit
crispr-cas9.subject: biology
crispr-cas9.title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing

crispr-cas9-target-recognition.shows: Toggle the PAM and move a guide mismatch along the target: Cas9 needs NGG, pairs the seed next to it first, and only a full R-loop leads to a cut
crispr-cas9-target-recognition.subject: biology
crispr-cas9-target-recognition.title: How Cas9 recognizes its target

crispr-dna-repair-outcomes.shows: Choose the repair pathway and the NHEJ indel size: indels that aren't a multiple of 3 shift the reading frame into an early stop codon, while HDR writes in the donor's exact change
crispr-dna-repair-outcomes.subject: biology
crispr-dna-repair-outcomes.title: Repairing a Cas9 cut: NHEJ or HDR

crispr-guide-directed-dna-cleavage.shows: Slide the guide along the DNA: Cas9 cuts only where an NGG PAM follows the matched 20 bases, always 3 bp from the PAM, with RuvC and HNH each cutting one strand
crispr-guide-directed-dna-cleavage.subject: biology
crispr-guide-directed-dna-cleavage.title: Guide-directed cutting by Cas9

currency-appreciation.shows: Pick an event and its size: demand for dollars rises or supply falls, the market clears at more euros per dollar, and the dollar appreciates
currency-appreciation.subject: finance
currency-appreciation.title: Why a currency appreciates

cytoskeletal-filament-comparison.shows: Pick a filament: actin (7 nm) and microtubules (25 nm) are polar, use ATP or GTP and carry motors, while intermediate filaments (10 nm) are unpolarized ropes built to bear tension
cytoskeletal-filament-comparison.subject: biology
cytoskeletal-filament-comparison.title: Three cytoskeletal filaments

cytotoxic-t-cell-infected-cell-killing.shows: Step through a kill: a CD8 T cell recognizes a viral peptide on MHC I, aims its granules and releases perforin and granzymes so the infected cell dies by apoptosis; a healthy cell is spared, and a cell hiding MHC I falls to an NK cell instead
cytotoxic-t-cell-infected-cell-killing.subject: biology
cytotoxic-t-cell-infected-cell-killing.title: Cytotoxic T cell killing

dcf.shows: Free cash flows grow for five years, each is discounted back to today, and they add up with the discounted terminal value into enterprise value
dcf.subject: finance
dcf.title: DCF: from free cash flows to enterprise value

degrees-of-freedom.shows: Fix the mean and drag the first n − 1 values: the last one is forced so the deviations sum to zero, which is why a sample variance divides by n − 1
degrees-of-freedom.subject: stats
degrees-of-freedom.title: Degrees of freedom: n − 1 free choices

dendritic-cell-antigen-presentation-help.shows: Step through it: a dendritic cell picks up antigen in a tissue, carries peptides on MHC II to a lymph node and gives a naive CD4 T cell three signals; without costimulation (B7) the T cell turns anergic, and the cytokines decide Th1, Th2 or Th17
dendritic-cell-antigen-presentation-help.subject: biology
dendritic-cell-antigen-presentation-help.title: Dendritic cell activates a helper T cell

density-dependent-contact-inhibition.shows: Run the days forward: normal cells fill the dish in one layer and stop dividing; cancer cells ignore the crowding and pile up
density-dependent-contact-inhibition.subject: biology
density-dependent-contact-inhibition.title: Density-dependent inhibition of cell division

desmosome-cell-anchoring.shows: Pull on the sheet: the force runs keratin, plaque, cadherins and back, so the junction holds; break the cadherins or the keratin and see where the tissue fails
desmosome-cell-anchoring.subject: biology
desmosome-cell-anchoring.title: Desmosomes: spot welds between cells

dice-rolling.shows: Add dice and rolls: the exact chance of each total is ways / 6^k (flat for one die, a triangle for two, a bell for more), and the rolled shares settle onto it
dice-rolling.subject: stats
dice-rolling.title: Rolling dice: chance vs what you see

difference-in-differences.shows: Set where each group starts, the trend they share and the policy's effect: the control's change stands in for what the treated group would have done, and the effect is what is left over
difference-in-differences.subject: stats
difference-in-differences.title: Difference-in-differences

direct-contact-cell-signaling.shows: Put the cells together or apart: a membrane-bound signal (Delta to Notch) or a gap junction only works while the cells touch
direct-contact-cell-signaling.subject: biology
direct-contact-cell-signaling.title: Signaling by direct contact

distance-traveled-vs-displacement.shows: Pick a route and scrub the trip: distance adds up every leg you walk, displacement is only the straight arrow from start to where you are, so a round trip ends with distance 280 m and displacement 0
distance-traveled-vs-displacement.subject: physics
distance-traveled-vs-displacement.title: Distance traveled vs displacement

dna-and-rna-structure.shows: Switch between DNA and RNA: two antiparallel strands versus one strand that folds back on itself; slide the G–C share to see the hydrogen bonds add up
dna-and-rna-structure.subject: biology
dna-and-rna-structure.title: DNA and RNA structure

dna-damage-repair-versus-apoptosis.shows: Step from damage to decision: sensors raise p53, a little p53 pauses the cycle for repair, a lot triggers apoptosis, and mutant p53 does neither
dna-damage-repair-versus-apoptosis.subject: biology
dna-damage-repair-versus-apoptosis.title: DNA damage: repair or apoptosis

dna-gel-fragment-migration.shows: Slide the run time and the fragment size: DNA runs toward +, small fragments run farther, and distance is a straight line against log size (log base 10)
dna-gel-fragment-migration.subject: biology
dna-gel-fragment-migration.title: Gel electrophoresis: how far a fragment runs

dna-methylation-transcriptional-silencin.shows: Methylate more of the promoter's CpGs: methyl groups block the transcription factor, MBD proteins bring in histone deacetylases, the chromatin closes and transcription stops
dna-methylation-transcriptional-silencin.subject: biology
dna-methylation-transcriptional-silencin.title: DNA methylation silences a gene

dna-replication.shows: Step through a replication fork: helicase opens it, primase lays RNA primers, polymerase builds the leading strand continuously and the lagging strand in Okazaki fragments, then pol I and ligase finish the job
dna-replication.subject: biology
dna-replication.title: DNA replication at the fork

dna-replication-antiparallel-template-po.shows: Flip the template's orientation and add nucleotides: the new strand always grows 5′→3′ off a 3′-OH, so it runs toward the fork on one template (leading) and away on the other (lagging)
dna-replication-antiparallel-template-po.subject: biology
dna-replication-antiparallel-template-po.title: Antiparallel strands: which way a new strand grows

dna-replication-five-prime-to-three-prim.shows: Step through one nucleotide being added: the strand's 3′-OH attacks the incoming dNTP's α-phosphate, pyrophosphate leaves, and the chain ends in a new 3′-OH, so it can only grow 5′ to 3′
dna-replication-five-prime-to-three-prim.subject: biology
dna-replication-five-prime-to-three-prim.title: Why a DNA strand grows 5′ to 3′

dna-replication-fork.shows: Slide time: the fork unzips the parent duplex and leaves two daughter duplexes behind it, each one old strand plus one new, the leading copy in one piece and the lagging copy in Okazaki fragments
dna-replication-fork.subject: biology
dna-replication-fork.title: The replication fork

dna-replication-fork-architecture.shows: Step through the machines at a replication fork (helicase, SSB, topoisomerase, primase, clamp and loader, two polymerases) and switch between E. coli and human names
dna-replication-fork-architecture.subject: biology
dna-replication-fork-architecture.title: The replisome: who does what at the fork

dna-replication-lagging-okazaki-fragment.shows: Slide the stretch copied and the fragment length: the lagging strand is built backward from the fork in Okazaki fragments, one primer each, and every join leaves a nick to seal
dna-replication-lagging-okazaki-fragment.subject: biology
dna-replication-lagging-okazaki-fragment.title: Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand

dna-replication-leading-lagging-strand-c.shows: Slide time at one fork: the leading strand grows in one piece right behind the helicase, while the lagging strand starts later, trails by one Okazaki fragment and stays in pieces
dna-replication-leading-lagging-strand-c.subject: biology
dna-replication-leading-lagging-strand-c.title: Leading and lagging strands compared

dna-replication-leading-strand-synthesis.shows: Slide time and toggle the sliding clamp: the leading strand follows the fork in one continuous piece from one primer, and the clamp is what keeps the polymerase on for the whole run
dna-replication-leading-strand-synthesis.subject: biology
dna-replication-leading-strand-synthesis.title: Leading strand: one primer, one continuous run

dna-replication-okazaki-fragment-joining.shows: Step through how two Okazaki fragments become one strand: the RNA primer between them is removed and replaced with DNA, leaving a nick that DNA ligase seals; switch between E. coli and human enzymes
dna-replication-okazaki-fragment-joining.subject: biology
dna-replication-okazaki-fragment-joining.title: Joining Okazaki fragments

dna-replication-origin-bidirectional-for.shows: Slide time on the E. coli chromosome: two forks leave oriC in opposite directions and meet at ter in about 38 minutes, half the time one fork would take; the bubble shows each fork's leading and lagging strand
dna-replication-origin-bidirectional-for.subject: biology
dna-replication-origin-bidirectional-for.title: One origin, two forks

dna-replication-polymerase-proofreading.shows: Step through a wrong base going in and the 3′→5′ exonuclease clipping it off; switch proofreading and mismatch repair off to see errors per genome copy jump
dna-replication-polymerase-proofreading.subject: biology
dna-replication-polymerase-proofreading.title: Proofreading: how DNA polymerase fixes its own mistakes

dna-replication-rna-primer-initiation.shows: Step through why polymerase needs a primer: primase lays RNA with a free 3′-OH, polymerase extends it, and the RNA is later swapped for DNA; slide the length copied to count primers
dna-replication-rna-primer-initiation.subject: biology
dna-replication-rna-primer-initiation.title: RNA primers: how DNA replication gets started

dna-replication-semiconservative-inherit.shows: Move heavy-labeled DNA into light medium for n generations: each model of copying predicts different bands in a density gradient, and only semiconservative matches what was seen
dna-replication-semiconservative-inherit.subject: biology
dna-replication-semiconservative-inherit.title: Semiconservative replication: the Meselson–Stahl result

dna-replication-versus-transcription-pro.shows: The same DNA, copied two ways: replication turns both strands of the whole molecule into two duplexes; transcription turns one strand of one gene into as many RNAs as the cell needs
dna-replication-versus-transcription-pro.subject: biology
dna-replication-versus-transcription-pro.title: Replication vs transcription: what each one makes

dna-rna-nucleotide-comparison.shows: Switch DNA and RNA and pick a base: the sugar differs by one oxygen on the 2′ carbon, and thymine is uracil with a methyl group
dna-rna-nucleotide-comparison.subject: biology
dna-rna-nucleotide-comparison.title: DNA and RNA nucleotides compared

dna-sequence-change-rna-message.shows: Change one base of a gene: see the new mRNA codon and the protein it makes, from a silent change to a missense, a premature stop or a frameshift
dna-sequence-change-rna-message.subject: biology
dna-sequence-change-rna-message.title: Mutations: from DNA to protein

dna-template-rna-complementarity.shows: Pick the template bases: each calls for its partner ribonucleotide (A pairs with U, not T), a purine always faces a pyrimidine, and G–C pairs add a third hydrogen bond
dna-template-rna-complementarity.subject: biology
dna-template-rna-complementarity.title: Template DNA and RNA: complementary base pairing

dna-transcription.shows: Step through one gene being transcribed in a bacterium or a eukaryote: polymerase finds the promoter, opens the DNA, builds RNA 5′→3′ off the template, and lets go at the end
dna-transcription.subject: biology
dna-transcription.title: Transcription: initiation, elongation, termination

dot-plot.shows: Pick a class: each dot is one student's count of books, so clusters, spread, gaps and unusual values show at a glance
dot-plot.subject: stats
dot-plot.title: Dot plot: shape, center and spread

dot-product-angle.shows: Drag u and v: u·v is |u| times the signed length of v's shadow on u, so it is positive for an acute angle, zero at 90° and negative past it
dot-product-angle.subject: linear-algebra
dot-product-angle.title: Dot product and the angle between vectors

double-entry-transaction-effects.shows: Pick a transaction: one account is debited and one credited, and Assets = Liabilities + Equity stays balanced after every entry
double-entry-transaction-effects.subject: finance
double-entry-transaction-effects.title: Double entry: one transaction, two accounts

eigendirections.shows: Change A and drag the probe x around the circle: Ax swings off x's line except along an eigendirection, where A only stretches by λ
eigendirections.subject: linear-algebra
eigendirections.title: Eigenvectors: the directions a matrix keeps

elementary-row-operations.shows: Step through swap, replace and scale: each row is a line, each operation moves a line, and the crossing point (the solution) never moves
elementary-row-operations.subject: linear-algebra
elementary-row-operations.title: Elementary row operations

elisa.shows: Step through the four layers of a sandwich ELISA; slide the antigen concentration: more antigen captured means more enzyme, more color, and a higher reading on the standard curve
elisa.subject: biology
elisa.title: Sandwich ELISA

empirical-rule.shows: Set the mean and SD: about 68% of a normal distribution lies within one SD of the mean, 95% within two and 99.7% within three
empirical-rule.subject: stats
empirical-rule.title: The empirical rule (68-95-99.7)

eukaryotic-enhancer-promoter-looping.shows: Move the enhancer near or far, upstream or downstream, and switch the activators or an insulator: the DNA loops so the enhancer touches the promoter through Mediator, unless nothing is bound or an insulator walls it off
eukaryotic-enhancer-promoter-looping.subject: biology
eukaryotic-enhancer-promoter-looping.title: Enhancers: DNA looping brings activators to the promoter

eukaryotic-gene-regulation.shows: Open or close the chromatin, bind an activator, add a microRNA or a degradation tag: each control point multiplies into how much mRNA and protein the cell ends up with
eukaryotic-gene-regulation.subject: biology
eukaryotic-gene-regulation.title: Eukaryotic gene regulation: control at every level

ev-equity-bridge.shows: Equity value plus debt, preferred and minority interest, minus cash, equals enterprise value; the balance-sheet view shows why cash comes off
ev-equity-bridge.subject: finance
ev-equity-bridge.title: Equity value to enterprise value

expected-value-weighted-average.shows: Change how many tickets carry each prize: E[X] weights every prize by its probability, so common prizes pull it toward them
expected-value-weighted-average.subject: stats
expected-value-weighted-average.title: Expected value as a weighted average

exponential-distribution.shows: Slide the rate and the wait: the density starts at λ and decays, the area past t is the chance of waiting longer than t, and the mean wait is 1/λ
exponential-distribution.subject: stats
exponential-distribution.title: Exponential distribution: waiting times

extracellular-matrix-structure.shows: Pull or squeeze the matrix, or remove one part: collagen bears tension, elastin recoils, the proteoglycan gel resists compression, and fibronectin and integrins tie it all to the cell's actin
extracellular-matrix-structure.subject: biology
extracellular-matrix-structure.title: The extracellular matrix

facilitated-diffusion-carrier.shows: Step a carrier through bind, flip and release, and change the glucose on each side: net flow runs down the gradient and levels off at Jₘₐₓ because each carrier can only turn over so fast
facilitated-diffusion-carrier.subject: biology
facilitated-diffusion-carrier.title: Facilitated diffusion: carrier proteins

facilitated-diffusion-channel.shows: Open or close a K⁺ channel and change the concentrations and membrane voltage: ions run through the pore down their electrochemical gradient, with no carrier cycle to saturate and no ATP
facilitated-diffusion-channel.subject: biology
facilitated-diffusion-channel.title: Facilitated diffusion: channel proteins

fifo-lifo-cost-flow.shows: Slide units sold and flip the cost trend: FIFO expenses the oldest batches first and LIFO the newest, so when costs move the two report different COGS and inventory
fifo-lifo-cost-flow.subject: finance
fifo-lifo-cost-flow.title: FIFO vs LIFO cost flow

fluid-mosaic-membrane.shows: A bilayer of phospholipids with cholesterol and proteins drifting in it: warm it, add kinked unsaturated tails or change the cholesterol, and watch the tails pack into a gel or loosen into a fluid
fluid-mosaic-membrane.subject: biology
fluid-mosaic-membrane.title: The fluid mosaic membrane

foreign-exchange-market.shows: Shift the demand for and supply of euros: the exchange rate settles where they cross, and the euro appreciates when demand rises or supply falls
foreign-exchange-market.subject: finance
foreign-exchange-market.title: The foreign exchange market

free-fall.shows: Set the starting height and speed, then scrub time: gravity takes 9.8 m/s off the velocity every second, so the height traces a downward parabola
free-fall.subject: physics
free-fall.title: Free fall: height against time

futures-hedge-locked-revenue.shows: Drag the harvest price: spot sales and the short futures move in opposite directions, so a full hedge always adds up to q times the futures price
futures-hedge-locked-revenue.subject: finance
futures-hedge-locked-revenue.title: Futures hedge: locking in revenue

g1-dna-damage-checkpoint-arrest.shows: Step through the G1 DNA damage checkpoint: ATM senses breaks, p53 builds up, p21 shuts off cyclin E–CDK2, Rb keeps E2F bound and the cell waits, repairs or dies; break p53 and the cell divides with damaged DNA
g1-dna-damage-checkpoint-arrest.subject: biology
g1-dna-damage-checkpoint-arrest.title: G1 checkpoint: DNA damage arrest

g2-replication-completion-checkpoint.shows: Slide how much of the DNA is copied: while any fork is still open, ATR and Chk1 keep cyclin B–CDK1 switched off and the cell waits in G2; finish replication, or block Chk1, and it enters mitosis
g2-replication-completion-checkpoint.subject: biology
g2-replication-completion-checkpoint.title: G2/M replication checkpoint

gap-junction-cell-communication.shows: Pick what cell 1 holds and whether the channels are open: ions and small molecules under about 1 kDa pass straight into the next cell through connexon pores and spread along the row; proteins are too big, and Ca²⁺ or acid closes the gates
gap-junction-cell-communication.subject: biology
gap-junction-cell-communication.title: Gap junctions: cell-to-cell channels

gel-electrophoresis-apparatus.shows: Set the voltage, the run time and which lead goes where: DNA is negative, so with black at the wells it runs toward red, at a speed set by the field V/L
gel-electrophoresis-apparatus.subject: biology
gel-electrophoresis-apparatus.title: Gel electrophoresis: the setup

gel-electrophoresis-size-separation.shows: Change the agarose percentage and run time: the gel mesh holds big fragments back, so a denser gel separates small fragments and a looser one separates large ones
gel-electrophoresis-size-separation.subject: biology
gel-electrophoresis-size-separation.title: Gel electrophoresis: separating by size

gene-coding-template-strand-orientation.shows: Pick a gene and slide transcription along it: the gene's direction decides the template, the strand that runs 3' to 5' the way RNA polymerase moves
gene-coding-template-strand-orientation.subject: biology
gene-coding-template-strand-orientation.title: Which strand is the template?

gene-expression-regulation.shows: Open or close the chromatin, add an activator and change the mRNA and protein half-lives: each stage multiplies how much protein the cell holds
gene-expression-regulation.subject: biology
gene-expression-regulation.title: Gene expression: control at every stage

genomic-imprinting-parent-of-origin.shows: Choose which parent's copy of an imprinted gene is read and who carries a deletion: marks are erased and reset in each parent's germline, so the child's fate depends on which parent passed the deletion on
genomic-imprinting-parent-of-origin.subject: biology
genomic-imprinting-parent-of-origin.title: Genomic imprinting: parent of origin

geometric-distribution.shows: Set the success chance and pick a trial: the first success lands on trial k only after k − 1 failures, so each bar is (1 − p) times the one before
geometric-distribution.subject: stats
geometric-distribution.title: Geometric distribution: waiting for the first success

golgi-apparatus-structure-and-sorting.shows: Pick a cargo and step it through: COPII vesicles bring it from the ER to the cis face, each cisterna edits its sugar chain, and the trans-Golgi network sends it out of the cell, into the membrane or to the lysosome, while ER proteins with KDEL are sent back
golgi-apparatus-structure-and-sorting.subject: biology
golgi-apparatus-structure-and-sorting.title: Golgi apparatus: processing and sorting

gpcr-signaling.shows: Pick Gs, Gi or Gq and step through: the ligand-bound receptor swaps GDP for GTP on Gα, the subunits split and change cAMP or Ca²⁺, and GTP hydrolysis switches the G protein off
gpcr-signaling.subject: biology
gpcr-signaling.title: GPCR signaling: Gs, Gi and Gq

helper-t-cell-coordinates-adaptive-immun.shows: Pick the helper subset and the CD4 count: a dendritic cell activates the CD4 T cell with three signals, the cytokines it then makes decide which cells it helps, and losing CD4 cells (as in HIV) takes that help away from all of them
helper-t-cell-coordinates-adaptive-immun.subject: biology
helper-t-cell-coordinates-adaptive-immun.title: Helper T cells coordinate adaptive immunity

heteroskedasticity.shows: Pick how the error spread behaves: constant spread leaves an even band of residuals, while a fan or a bulge is heteroskedasticity, and White's test picks it up
heteroskedasticity.subject: stats
heteroskedasticity.title: Heteroskedasticity: when the spread changes

histogram.shows: Pick a shape and a bin width: the bars count scores per interval, so symmetry, a long tail, two peaks or a gap with an outlier show up, unless the bins are too wide
histogram.subject: stats
histogram.title: Histogram: the shape of a distribution

histone-acetylation-chromatin-opening.shows: Step through it: positive lysines on the histone tails hold DNA tight, acetyl groups from a HAT cancel those charges so the chromatin opens and the gene is read, and HDACs remove them again unless an HDAC inhibitor blocks them
histone-acetylation-chromatin-opening.subject: biology
histone-acetylation-chromatin-opening.title: Histone acetylation opens chromatin

hookes-law.shows: Drag the block or slide k and x: the spring's force always points back toward x = 0 and is k times as big as the stretch
hookes-law.subject: physics
hookes-law.title: Hooke's law: the spring pulls back

humoral-versus-cell-mediated-immunity.shows: Pick a threat: antibodies from B cells (humoral) work in blood and lymph on toxins, bacteria and free virus, while T cells (cell-mediated) kill infected cells or arm macrophages against microbes hiding inside cells
humoral-versus-cell-mediated-immunity.subject: biology
humoral-versus-cell-mediated-immunity.title: Humoral versus cell-mediated immunity

hypergeometric-distribution.shows: Set the population, its successes and the sample size, then pick k: the chance is the number of samples with exactly k successes over all samples of n
hypergeometric-distribution.subject: stats
hypergeometric-distribution.title: Hypergeometric distribution: drawing without replacement

immune-acute-inflammation-neutrophil-rec.shows: Step a neutrophil out of an inflamed venule: selectins capture it, it rolls, a chemokine switches its integrins on, it stops on ICAM-1 and squeezes through to the bacteria; switch on LAD I or LAD II to see which step fails
immune-acute-inflammation-neutrophil-rec.subject: biology
immune-acute-inflammation-neutrophil-rec.title: Neutrophil recruitment: the adhesion cascade

immune-cell-phagocytosis.shows: Step a phagocyte through eating a bacterium: receptors grip it, pseudopods wrap it into a phagosome, lysosomes and the oxidative burst kill it, and a macrophage shows its pieces to T cells; switch off NADPH oxidase to see chronic granulomatous disease
immune-cell-phagocytosis.subject: biology
immune-cell-phagocytosis.title: Phagocytosis: engulf, fuse, kill

immune-memory-secondary-response.shows: Set the size of the memory pool, how fast memory cells get going and how fast cells divide: the second response clears the detection line sooner because it skips the slow start and needs fewer doublings
immune-memory-secondary-response.subject: biology
immune-memory-secondary-response.title: Immune memory: why the second response is faster

inclined-plane-acceleration.shows: Tilt the slope or change the mass: the pull down the slope is mg sin θ, so the acceleration is g sin θ and the mass cancels out
inclined-plane-acceleration.subject: physics
inclined-plane-acceleration.title: Sliding down a frictionless incline

independent-probability-intersection.shows: Drag the corner or slide P(A) and P(B): for independent events the overlap is a rectangle, so its area is P(A) times P(B)
independent-probability-intersection.subject: stats
independent-probability-intersection.title: Independent events: multiply the probabilities

joint-marginal-conditional-table.shows: Pick a question about the 120 students: the amber count goes on top, and the blue group it is counted out of goes underneath
joint-marginal-conditional-table.subject: stats
joint-marginal-conditional-table.title: Joint, marginal and conditional probability

kaplan-meier-survival-curve.shows: Step through the event times: each event multiplies the curve by 1 − d/n of those still at risk, while a censored subject just leaves the risk set
kaplan-meier-survival-curve.subject: stats
kaplan-meier-survival-curve.title: Kaplan-Meier survival curve

kernel-image.shows: Drag x in the input plane: T(x) moves in the output plane; the kernel line is crushed to 0 and the image is the set T can reach
kernel-image.subject: linear-algebra
kernel-image.title: Kernel and image of a linear map

kinematics-displacement-uniform-accelera.shows: Slide vᵢ, a and t: the area under the velocity line is a rectangle vᵢ·t plus a triangle ½at², and together they are the displacement
kinematics-displacement-uniform-accelera.subject: physics
kinematics-displacement-uniform-accelera.title: Displacement under constant acceleration

kinematics-position.shows: Slide vᵢ, a and t: under constant acceleration the average velocity is the plain average of the start and end velocities, so the trapezoid under the line equals a rectangle v̄·t
kinematics-position.subject: physics
kinematics-position.title: Displacement from average velocity

kinematics-velocity.shows: Slide v_i, a and t: the velocity line starts at v_i, climbs by a every second, and after t seconds has gained a·t
kinematics-velocity.subject: physics
kinematics-velocity.title: Velocity under constant acceleration

kinematics-velocity-squared.shows: Slide v_i, a and Δx: speed squared behaves like area, so 2aΔx adds (or cuts) a strip and the new square's side is v_f
kinematics-velocity-squared.subject: physics
kinematics-velocity-squared.title: Speed squared over a distance

kinesin-dynein-vesicle-transport.shows: Switch the motor and spend ATP: kinesin walks to the microtubule's plus end, out to the axon tip; dynein walks to the minus end, back to the cell body; about 8 nm per ATP
kinesin-dynein-vesicle-transport.subject: biology
kinesin-dynein-vesicle-transport.title: Kinesin and dynein: vesicle transport

kinetic-and-potential-energy.shows: Drop the ball and step down: potential energy mgh drains into kinetic energy ½mv² while their total stays mgh₀
kinetic-and-potential-energy.subject: physics
kinetic-and-potential-energy.title: Potential energy into kinetic energy

kinetic-energy.shows: Slide the mass and the velocity: KE = ½mv² grows with the square of the speed, and the direction of motion doesn't matter
kinetic-energy.subject: physics
kinetic-energy.title: Kinetic energy

lac-operon.shows: Toggle glucose and lactose: lactose takes the repressor off the operator, low glucose lets CAP-cAMP help RNA polymerase, and only lactose without glucose turns the genes fully on
lac-operon.subject: biology
lac-operon.title: The lac operon: lactose and glucose

lac-operon-catabolite-activation.shows: Toggle glucose, the strain and added cAMP: low glucose raises cAMP, CAP-cAMP binds beside the lac promoter and helps RNA polymerase start about 50 times more often
lac-operon-catabolite-activation.subject: biology
lac-operon-catabolite-activation.title: lac operon: CAP and cAMP

lac-operon-inducer-repression-switch.shows: Raise the inducer (IPTG): it binds the lac repressor, which lets go of the operator, and expression climbs a steep S-curve; lacI⁻ and Oᶜ stay on, lacIˢ never turns on
lac-operon-inducer-repression-switch.subject: biology
lac-operon-inducer-repression-switch.title: lac repressor: the inducer switch

lbo-returns.shows: Entry multiple, leverage, EBITDA growth and exit multiple turn into the equity's MOIC and IRR, split into growth, multiple and debt paydown
lbo-returns.subject: finance
lbo-returns.title: LBO returns: IRR and MOIC

least-square-regression.shows: Move the trial line: each residual becomes a square, and the least squares line is the one with the smallest total area
least-square-regression.subject: stats
least-square-regression.title: Least squares regression line

likelihood-function.shows: Set the successes and trials: the likelihood p^k(1−p)^(n−k) peaks at p̂ = k/n and narrows as the trials grow
likelihood-function.subject: stats
likelihood-function.title: Likelihood of a success probability

linear-combination.shows: Slide a and b, or drag w: w = a u + b v is a walk of a steps along u then b steps along v; negative coefficients walk backwards
linear-combination.subject: linear-algebra
linear-combination.title: Linear combination of two vectors

linear-independence-discriminant.shows: Drag u and v: the parallelogram they span has area |det(u, v)|; when it collapses to zero the two vectors are dependent and span only a line
linear-independence-discriminant.subject: linear-algebra
linear-independence-discriminant.title: Span and linear independence

logistic-regression.shows: Slide β₀ and β₁: the log-odds β₀ + β₁x is a straight line, and the logistic function bends it into a probability between 0 and 1
logistic-regression.subject: stats
logistic-regression.title: Logistic regression curve

lymphocyte-development-recirculation.shows: Pick T or B cells and step through a life: born in the bone marrow, tested in the thymus or marrow, then blood, lymph node, lymph and back to blood until they meet their antigen
lymphocyte-development-recirculation.subject: biology
lymphocyte-development-recirculation.title: Lymphocytes: development and recirculation

mass-spring-shm.shows: Slide the mass, stiffness and amplitude: the period T = 2π√(m/k) depends on m and k only, never on how far it swings
mass-spring-shm.subject: physics
mass-spring-shm.title: Mass on a spring: simple harmonic motion

matched-pairs-design.shows: Pair similar units (or use each unit twice) and analyse the differences: between-unit spread drops out of the comparison
matched-pairs-design.subject: stats
matched-pairs-design.title: Matched pairs design

matrix-inverse-2d.shows: Change A and x: A moves the grid and x into the output plane, and A⁻¹ = (1/det A)·[d −b; −c a] brings Ax back to x, unless det A = 0
matrix-inverse-2d.subject: linear-algebra
matrix-inverse-2d.title: The inverse of a 2×2 matrix

matrix-multiplication-row-column-rule.shows: Step through AB: each entry c_ij is row i of A dotted with column j of B, so the inner sizes must match
matrix-multiplication-row-column-rule.subject: linear-algebra
matrix-multiplication-row-column-rule.title: Matrix multiplication: the row-column rule

matrix-of-a-map.shows: The columns of the matrix are the images of the basis vectors
matrix-of-a-map.subject: linear-algebra
matrix-of-a-map.title: The matrix of a linear map

matrix-transformation-2d.shows: Change the entries of A: the columns are where e1 and e2 land, the grid moves with them, and det A scales areas
matrix-transformation-2d.subject: linear-algebra
matrix-transformation-2d.title: A matrix as a map of the plane

mature-mrna-structure.shows: Step from the 5′ cap to the poly(A) tail of a spliced mRNA and change the lengths: only the stretch from AUG to the stop codon is translated, 3 nt per amino acid
mature-mrna-structure.subject: biology
mature-mrna-structure.title: Mature mRNA: cap, UTRs, coding sequence, tail

mean-as-balance-point.shows: Move the fulcrum: the beam balances only at the mean, where the distances to the left and right weigh the same
mean-as-balance-point.subject: stats
mean-as-balance-point.title: The mean as a balance point

mean-vs-median.shows: Add one extreme score: the mean is pulled toward it, while the median, the middle value, barely moves
mean-vs-median.subject: stats
mean-vs-median.title: Mean vs median

mediation-indirect-effect.shows: Set the paths a, b and c′: the indirect effect is a × b, and the total effect of X on Y is c = c′ + ab
mediation-indirect-effect.subject: stats
mediation-indirect-effect.title: Mediation: direct and indirect effects

membrane-bilayer-polarity.shows: Move an ion through the bilayer: polar heads face the water on both sides, the tails make a nonpolar core, and the energy to put a charge there climbs to about 170 kJ/mol (Born model)
membrane-bilayer-polarity.subject: biology
membrane-bilayer-polarity.title: Bilayer polarity: polar faces, nonpolar core

membrane-channel-carrier-specificity.shows: Pick a protein, a solute and a concentration: a K⁺ channel sorts by size and charge in its filter and runs at millions per second; a glucose carrier sorts by shape, flips for every molecule and tops out near 10³
membrane-channel-carrier-specificity.subject: biology
membrane-channel-carrier-specificity.title: Channels vs carriers: how each picks its solute

membrane-selective-permeability.shows: Pick a molecule and a cell size: gases cross bare lipid in microseconds, water and urea in seconds to minutes, glucose in weeks and ions in years, which is why cells need transport proteins
membrane-selective-permeability.subject: biology
membrane-selective-permeability.title: Selective permeability of the lipid bilayer

meta-analysis.shows: Spread the six study results apart: heterogeneity (I², τ²) grows, and random effects evens out the weights and widens the pooled interval
meta-analysis.subject: stats
meta-analysis.title: Meta-analysis: fixed vs random effects

meta-analysis-forest-weights.shows: Change the study weights or drag a result: the pooled effect is the weighted mean, pulled toward the heaviest, most precise studies
meta-analysis-forest-weights.subject: stats
meta-analysis-forest-weights.title: Forest plot: how weights pool studies

mhc-i-vs-mhc-ii-presentation.shows: Step both routes side by side: inside proteins go proteasome, TAP, ER and MHC I to CD8 T cells; engulfed proteins go endosome, CLIP swap and MHC II to CD4 T cells
mhc-i-vs-mhc-ii-presentation.subject: biology
mhc-i-vs-mhc-ii-presentation.title: MHC I vs MHC II: two routes to the surface

microrna-mrna-translational-silencing.shows: Step from Dicer to silencing and change the sites in the 3′ UTR: seed-paired miRNAs trim the tail and block translation, a little more per site; a full match lets Argonaute slice the mRNA
microrna-mrna-translational-silencing.subject: biology
microrna-mrna-translational-silencing.title: MicroRNA silencing of an mRNA

microtubule-polarity-and-growth.shows: Slide the free tubulin and switch each end between growth and catastrophe: the beta-exposed plus end grows about twice as fast as the minus end while its GTP cap lasts, and either end shrinks over ten times faster than it grows once the cap is lost
microtubule-polarity-and-growth.subject: biology
microtubule-polarity-and-growth.title: Microtubule polarity and dynamic instability

mitochondrion-structure-and-atp-producti.shows: The folded inner membrane carries the electron transport chain: complexes I, III and IV pump 10 protons per NADH into the intermembrane space and ATP synthase spends about 4 per ATP; change the shuttle, let protons leak or block complex IV and watch the yield per glucose
mitochondrion-structure-and-atp-producti.subject: biology
mitochondrion-structure-and-atp-producti.title: Mitochondrion: structure and ATP production

mitosis.shows: Step a cell with 2n chromosomes through prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase: duplicated chromosomes line up, sister chromatids split to opposite poles, and each daughter ends with the same 2n chromosomes as the mother
mitosis.subject: biology
mitosis.title: Mitosis: one cell becomes two

mitosis-chromosome-segregation.shows: Pick how one chromosome's sister kinetochores attach and step through anaphase: an unattached or tensionless kinetochore keeps the checkpoint on and anaphase waits; bi-orientation lets separase cut cohesin; a merotelic chromatid slips past the checkpoint and lags
mitosis-chromosome-segregation.subject: biology
mitosis-chromosome-segregation.title: Chromosome segregation and the spindle checkpoint

mitosis-phase-sequence-overview.shows: Step through prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase and cytokinesis: what the envelope, the chromosomes and the spindle do in each, and how M phase is only about an hour of a 24-hour cycle
mitosis-phase-sequence-overview.subject: biology
mitosis-phase-sequence-overview.title: Mitosis: the phases in order

momentum.shows: Set the masses and speed: cart 1 brings momentum m1·v, and after the collision the carts share exactly that much
momentum.subject: physics
momentum.title: Momentum in a collision

mosaic-plot.shows: Change the four counts: tile areas are the counts, and when the splits line up across columns the two variables are independent
mosaic-plot.subject: stats
mosaic-plot.title: Mosaic plot of a two-way table

motile-cilium-axoneme-structure.shows: Bend the cilium: dynein arms on one half of the 9+2 ring push their neighbors toward the tip, nexin links turn that sliding into a bend with tip offset d times theta, and with the links digested the doublets just slide apart
motile-cilium-axoneme-structure.subject: biology
motile-cilium-axoneme-structure.title: Motile cilium: the 9+2 axoneme

mrna-codon-amino-acid-sequence.shows: Change one base or shift the reading frame: the mRNA is read three bases at a time from AUG, each codon names an amino acid, and a stop codon ends the chain
mrna-codon-amino-acid-sequence.subject: biology
mrna-codon-amino-acid-sequence.title: Reading an mRNA: codons to amino acids

mrna-translation.shows: Step the ribosome along the mRNA: tRNAs pair with each codon, the chain moves onto the newest amino acid, and a stop codon ends it; try a one-base mutation
mrna-translation.subject: biology
mrna-translation.title: Translation: mRNA to protein

mutation-base-substitution.shows: Change one base in the start of the beta-globin gene: the new codon may still code for the same amino acid, swap it for another (GAG to GTG gives the sickle-cell Glu6Val) or become a stop; and A-G or C-T swaps are transitions, the rest transversions
mutation-base-substitution.subject: biology
mutation-base-substitution.title: Base substitution: silent, missense or nonsense

mutation-codon-reading-frame.shows: Move the start base: the ribosome cuts the same mRNA into triplets from there, so starts 1, 4, 7 share one frame and starts 2 or 3 read different codons and a different chain
mutation-codon-reading-frame.subject: biology
mutation-codon-reading-frame.title: Reading frames: where the codons start

mutation-deletion-frameshift.shows: Delete one or two bases anywhere after the start codon: every later base slides left, the triplets regroup, and the chain is wrong from there until a premature stop
mutation-deletion-frameshift.subject: biology
mutation-deletion-frameshift.title: Deletion frameshift

mutation-dna-rna-protein-phenotype.shows: Change codon 6 of beta-globin and follow it down: DNA, mRNA, protein, hemoglobin and red cells; GAG to GTG makes HbS, which sickles cells when oxygen is low
mutation-dna-rna-protein-phenotype.subject: biology
mutation-dna-rna-protein-phenotype.title: From DNA to trait: one base in beta-globin

mutation-frameshift-versus-in-frame.shows: Add or remove 1 to 6 bases after codon 4: only multiples of 3 keep the triplets in step, so the protein just gains or loses amino acids; any other size garbles everything after the site until a stop
mutation-frameshift-versus-in-frame.subject: biology
mutation-frameshift-versus-in-frame.title: Frameshift or in frame?

mutation-in-frame-indels.shows: Delete or duplicate 3 or 6 bases in the CFTR gene: the frame survives, so the protein just loses or gains whole amino acids (CTT gone is F508del, the common cystic fibrosis allele)
mutation-in-frame-indels.subject: biology
mutation-in-frame-indels.title: In-frame insertions and deletions

mutation-insertion-frameshift.shows: Insert one or two bases anywhere after the start codon: every later base slides right, the triplets regroup, and the chain is wrong from there until a premature stop
mutation-insertion-frameshift.subject: biology
mutation-insertion-frameshift.title: Insertion frameshift

mutation-missense-substitution.shows: Change one base in the first codons of beta-globin: a missense change swaps one amino acid, and how much it matters depends on whether the new side chain is like the old one (GAG to GTG is the sickle-cell Glu6Val)
mutation-missense-substitution.subject: biology
mutation-missense-substitution.title: Missense substitution

mutation-nonsense-premature-stop.shows: Slide a premature stop codon along the beta-globin gene: the chain is cut short at that codon, and a stop well before the last exon junction gets the mRNA destroyed by nonsense-mediated decay
mutation-nonsense-premature-stop.subject: biology
mutation-nonsense-premature-stop.title: Nonsense mutation: a premature stop

mutations.shows: Substitute, insert or delete bases anywhere in a short gene: one changed codon is silent, missense or nonsense, while inserting or deleting anything but a multiple of 3 bases shifts the reading frame and garbles everything downstream until a stop
mutations.subject: biology
mutations.title: Mutations: substitutions and frameshifts

newton-first-law.shows: Give the puck a speed and a surface: with no net force it keeps the same velocity forever; friction is a net force and slows it to a stop
newton-first-law.subject: physics
newton-first-law.title: Newton's first law: inertia

newton-second-law.shows: Change the net force and the mass: the acceleration is F/m, so it grows in step with the force and shrinks as the mass grows
newton-second-law.subject: physics
newton-second-law.title: Newton's second law: F = ma

newton-third-law.shows: Pick an interaction and set its force: each object pushes the other with the same size force in the opposite direction, acting on different objects
newton-third-law.subject: physics
newton-third-law.title: Newton's third law: interaction pairs

normal-approximation-to-binomial.shows: Set n, p and an event: the bell curve with the same mean and SD stands in for the binomial bars, with k ± 0.5 as the continuity correction
normal-approximation-to-binomial.subject: stats
normal-approximation-to-binomial.title: Normal approximation to the binomial

null-space.shows: Change the rank of a 3×3 matrix: the solutions of Ax = 0 shrink from a plane to a line to just 0 while the columns grow from a line to a plane to all of space
null-space.subject: linear-algebra
null-space.title: Null space and column space

ogive.shows: Pick a percentile: read across from it to the cumulative frequency curve and down to the value; steep stretches are where the data are dense
ogive.subject: stats
ogive.title: Ogive: cumulative frequency

one-sample-t-test.shows: Set the sample's mean, SD and size against a hypothesized mean: t counts standard errors from μ0, and the shaded tail is the p-value
one-sample-t-test.subject: stats
one-sample-t-test.title: One-sample t test

outlier-leverage-influence.shows: Drag the amber point: leverage grows with its distance from x̄, the residual with its distance from the trend, and only together do they swing the line
outlier-leverage-influence.subject: stats
outlier-leverage-influence.title: Outliers, leverage and influence

paired-t-test.shows: Each student is measured twice: the test runs on the differences, so t is the mean change over its standard error
paired-t-test.subject: stats
paired-t-test.title: Paired t test

pcr-cycle.shows: Step through denature, anneal and extend on one template; slide the cycle count to see the copies double every cycle
pcr-cycle.subject: biology
pcr-cycle.title: PCR: one cycle, then doubling
